findings.problem: Every one of the 16 theorems contains five copies (hm0–hm4, 80 blocks in total) of the same argument. Each copy applies familyPairMoment_of_pointwise, introduces H hH, proves groupedColumns node (family3.label k) = raw… by rewriting with groupedColumns_family3_k, using Matrix.ext, unfolding and running decide +kernel, rewrites with that equality, and closes with (canonical… hH).trans (sound… hH). Only the node, the label index k, the raw matrix, and the canonical/sound/value names change. The `have hp … rw [← hl] at hp … rw [hm0,…] at hp; norm_num …; linarith` frame is also repeated verbatim 16 times. The file is about 1000 lines, and a change to the proof pattern (for example the lemma used for grouping) would need 80 edits.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma before the first theorem (or in PairAverage.lean):

theorem familyPairMoment_of_canonical {p q r n : ℕ} (B : Fin 7 → Basis) (hB : IsMUBFamily B)
    (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin n) ℤ) (R : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin n) ℤ) (N : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin n) ℤ)
    (v : Sparse (Fin 909)) (hA : A = R)
    (hcan : ∀ {H : CMatrix}, IsHadamard H → injectiveMoment H R = injectiveMoment H N)
    (hsound : ∀ {H : CMatrix}, IsHadamard H → injectiveMoment H N = Sparse.eval v (PairSemantics.momentVector H)) :
    familyPairMoment B A = Sparse.eval v (familyPairVector B) := by
  subst hA
  exact familyPairMoment_of_pointwise B hB _ v fun H hH => (hcan hH).trans (hsound hH)

(The statement as written needs the shapes of the canonical/sound lemmas to match. The existing lemmas have an implicit H and an hH argument, so they fit after adjusting binder style.)

Proof sketch: this is just familyPairMoment_of_pointwise plus transitivity of the canonical and sound equalities. Each block then becomes

  have hm0 : familyPairMoment B (groupedColumns node136 (EqualityPatterns.family3.label 0)) =
      Sparse.eval PairSemantics.value0 (familyPairVector B) :=
    familyPairMoment_of_canonical B hB _ PairSemantics.raw7980 PairSemantics.node0 _
      (by rw [groupedColumns_family3_0]; apply Matrix.ext; unfold node136 PairSemantics.raw7980; decide +kernel)
      PairSemantics.canonical7980 PairSemantics.sound0

and likewise for hm1 (raw5116, node45, canonical5116, sound45, via groupedColumns_family3_1) through hm4. Under the same hypotheses (B, hB, node136 of type Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 3) ℤ), this gives the same hm0..hm4 statements, so the later `rw [hm0, …] at hp`, norm_num and linarith lines are unchanged. For singlePair137 the call is identical with node137 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 3) ℤ, raw7981, value118 and so on. The helper is generic in the row counts p, q, r, so both nodes use it.

Optionally, bundle the `hp`/`hl` prologue and the norm_num/linarith epilogue into a second lemma that takes the five hm hypotheses as arguments. Each singlePair theorem would then only list its five (raw, canonical, sound) triples.
findings.benefit: Each theorem shrinks from about 60 lines to about 25, and the file from roughly 1080 lines to about 450. The mathematical content of each case (which raw matrix and which canonical/sound lemma per label) is visible at a glance instead of being buried in boilerplate. A change to how pointwise results are lifted to the family average is made once. The risk of a copy-paste mismatch (for example a wrong raw index in a heq versus the canonical lemma) is reduced, because the lemma's types force raw/canonical/sound to line up.
